approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a score-ranked population, using crossover and mutation with stable canonical identity checks. It keeps every accepted raw score, refits a Gaussian process on local molecular environment counts, and draws whole prediction functions over a fresh surplus pool. Each requested evaluation goes to the best still-available candidate under one function draw. Accepted outcomes update the archive, raw-score survivors and future breeding population.
approach.novelty: Replace that learner and its sampled functions together with a fixed ensemble of bootstrapped regression trees on exactly the same count vectors. Refit all trees from accepted labels, then choose each evaluation using one uniformly sampled tree over the full pool. This tests a different nonlinear response law after kernel, target, residual-scale and acquisition variants failed. The trees can disagree, but bounded leaf averages and exact ties can also limit exploration; both are measured rather than repaired during the test.

hypothesis: Replace the active accepted-only count-GP learner and Gaussian function distribution jointly with 128 fixed bootstrapped CART response trees on unchanged Morgan counts, allocating each batch position by the maximum of one uniformly sampled tree function with replacement and original-index exact ties.

finding_summary.headline: Tree functions changed every selected batch, but the paired endpoint mean fell by 0.060977
finding_summary.insights:
Distinct fitted functions and changed evaluation choices were not sufficient for endpoint benefit. Selected-stream mean squared error improved from 0.012718 to 0.010939, while ordering correlation fell from 0.5322 to 0.4474. Every median_2 error improved even though all its endpoints declined. These are different adaptive evaluation streams, so neither the lower error nor the empirical tree spread establishes calibration or explains the total loss. Exact ties, leaf-average support and later search history remain possible contributors whose individual effects were not isolated.

The inherited inputs still merge some distinct molecules: nineteen current alias pairs were observed, but only one pair had both members scored, at an equal value. Trees additionally give equal predictions to many unequal count vectors. Neither representation aliases nor shared leaves prove chemical identity or independent scaffold coverage. Conventional compact indole amides, carbon-bound halogens and available amines coexist with giant linked-ring structures, reactive bonds and difficult bridges. Useful conventional counterexamples rule out a universal need for those liabilities; they do not establish a chemical cause of the score loss.

This result concerns the joint fixed learner and sampled-function law. It does not reverse the useful GP boundary or its conditional component findings, and it does not identify separate effects of trees, bootstrapping, ties or uncertainty. The large runtime spread is preserved: all replicas completed under identical resources, with much of the observed elapsed variation in deco_hop oracle time. Changed molecules and nested instrumentation prevent an isolated learner-speed or chemistry attribution.
finding_summary.results:
All 435 accepted-archive refits and all 55,680 native tree structures reproduced. Every pool contained 128 distinct functions with 7 to 47 distinct first maximizers, and all 435 selected sets differed from both ensemble-mean and generation-order controls. Selection still relied heavily on pool order: 4,092 of 4,350 sampled-function maxima were exact ties. One unselected tree was constant; no entire batch lacked functional exposure. Real feedback remained intact, with 581 parent wins and 252 incumbent advances, compared with 629 and 258 for the Parent.

The complete three-seed mean fell from 0.595670 to 0.534693, a paired loss of 0.060977 against the required gain of 0.002. Seed changes were −0.082304, +0.000169 and −0.100795. Five task/seed endpoints improved: deco_hop seeds 1 and 2, drd2 seed 1, sitagliptin seed 1 and zaleplon seed 2. Ten declined; all five task means and all three median_2 endpoints were lower. The implemented mechanism is confirmed and its endpoint-benefit prediction is falsified.

molecular.headline: Compact aromatic amides and amines coexist with giant linked heterocycles, reactive heteroatom bonds and difficult bridges
molecular.overall_character: All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent task/seed trajectories were read: 4,500 observations per arm, including 4,350 evaluated optimizer offspring per arm. All five tasks and issued Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 are covered; context.comparison reports complete Child evaluation and complete matched Parent pairing with n-62daf219c70a. No required trajectory or comparison is absent. The output contains indole anilides, aza-aromatic ketones and thioamides, repeated nitrogen-dione systems, extended polyaryl lactones, cyclic aryl amines, bridged nitrogen-carbonyl frameworks and fluorinated imino/enol heterocycles. There is abundant ring chemistry: digest ring-closure incidence is 0.9977 to 1.0 and aromatic-text incidence 0.9839 to 1.0 across evaluated optimizer proposals. These are incidences of SMILES text features, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Compact leaders with 23 to 35 heavy-atom tokens coexist with two linked-heterocycle leaders with 104 and 115 tokens. Size statements count heavy-atom tokens in actual SMILES; no conformation or synthesis calculation was performed. Ring systems and aromaticity are rich, synthetic plausibility is questionable and drug-likeness weak overall. Recognizable amides, carbon-bound halogens, ethers and amines provide favorable conventional counterexamples, but other high-scoring structures retain N-halogen or O-Cl bonds, unusual sulfur valence, very short bridges, crowded unsaturation or enormous repeated aromatic regions. Diversity is moderate across tasks and seeds, with narrower related families among leaders within a seed; distinct strings, folded fingerprints and tree predictions do not establish independent scaffold coverage. Every task has zero stereocentre and formal-charge text incidence. Potentially stereogenic and protonatable structures nevertheless occur; unspecified identity is not evidence of absent amines or a measured protonation/stereochemical penalty. The accepted-provenance audit joins each of the 4,350 observed offspring to its same-batch emitted identity, sampled function selection and earlier real breeding-parent observations. All fifteen first endpoint leaders were immediately admitted to survival. Immediate admission is not a claim about every later population. Initial molecules are identified separately; trajectory final rows are late evaluations, not necessarily retained leaders. The selector is the joint replacement of the learner and function-sampling law by 128 native bootstrap CART trees on inherited folded Morgan occurrence counts, with one uniformly sampled fitted tree function per batch position. Predictions are in raw-score units; logged spread is empirical tree-population dispersion, not Gaussian posterior uncertainty or established calibration. The raw accepted scores and endpoint definition remain unchanged. In the current logs, 4,092 of 4,350 selected available maxima are tied and are resolved by original pool order. This is descriptive selection provenance, not evidence that tied molecules are identical or that order, bagging or any isolated constituent caused endpoint behavior. Count aliases can persist, and different count vectors can also share tree leaves. Unselected pool candidates, passive mean choices and alternative tree choices have no counterfactual oracle labels or independent rollout here. The inherited breeding, ordinary mutation/crossover, identity rules and raw-score survival remain relevant to the observed families. A matched whole-node Parent comparison does not isolate the chemical contribution of the learner, bootstrap, function law or inherited components. Published Parent chemistry is the comparison baseline; its carried gaps originated in n-c55c3d520a2c and were reproduced by the same-code n-62daf219c70a baseline, not independently rediscovered there. The current panel supplies new conditional chemistry observations without rewriting that history. The successful resource receipt records 6 CPUs, one A40 and 16,000 MB for each replica, with elapsed times 00:41:07, 00:05:05 and 00:49:55. Their spread is retained as execution context without chemical or computational causal attribution. Scores and structural associations below do not establish synthesis, stability, conformation, biological activity, mechanism activation or eligibility. Evidence and reproducible audits are in .slots/r0020-01-improve-L01/molecular/trajectory_audit.json and accepted_provenance_audit.json; source hashes include the immutable brief, current logs, Parent evidence and resource receipt.

per_task.generated_character: All 870 evaluated optimizer proposals contain ring-closure and aromatic text; halogen incidence is 0.9586. Seed 0 evaluation 203 is a compact 23-token dimethyl/hydroxymethyl N-H indole anilide with carbon-bound fluorine and an ordinary secondary amide. This is a comparatively plausible conventional counterexample to a universal reactive-bond requirement. Seed 1 evaluation 299 is another 23-token structure, an aza-aromatic fused/partially unsaturated system bearing a ketone-linked fluoroethylpyridyl group rather than an amide. Seed 2 evaluation 292 has 26 tokens, vinyl/alkyl substitution, an N-hydroxy fused nitrogen ring and an N-chloroamide linked to fluoropyridine. Thus the three leaders are not one identical scaffold or bond environment. The seed-0 leader was emitted from logged crossover of two earlier accepted molecules and retained; the seed-1 leader from crossover plus ring opening; the seed-2 leader from an append-atom event on the accepted N-H/N-chloroamide relative at evaluation 242. These are actual lineage observations, not isolated causal comparisons.
liabilities: N-F and N-Cl amides and N-hydroxy aromatic nitrogen raise bond-environment and stability questions; their observed scores do not establish makeability.
Large linked aromatic amides consume evaluations at extremely low scores even though all proposals remain ring-containing and aromatic; this panel is not chiefly a failure to generate rings.
missing_features: Coverage remains incomplete for compact, geometrically credible alternatives that retain the favorable aromatic/carbonyl arrangement without reactive N-halogen or congested ring modifications; the conventional seed-0 leader demonstrates partial access already.
The records do not resolve stereochemical or conformational identity for newly constrained ring systems, and do not identify one missing substituent that would close the endpoint difference.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole anilide at seed 0 evaluation 9 scores 0.3051048083696145; the hydroxymethyl/dimethyl anilide leader scores 0.3940393921126993. The seed-1 ketone leader scores 0.41429901422917714, so an amide or N-halogen bond is not universally required for a favorable score in these samples. Seed-2 evaluations 131 and 184 replace N-F with N-Cl but tie exactly at 0.4387992465191; the later N-hydroxy/N-chloroamide leader scores 0.4514335070299504. This does not isolate the benefit of either bond. In contrast, the 48-token linked bis-amide at seed 2 evaluation 159 scores 1.1392566875964384e-25, and the 51-token linked aromatic amide at seed 1 evaluation 97 scores 7.650532204801377e-25. Even the later extra-pyridyl relative at seed 2 evaluation 295 scores only 0.10241332625357968. The observed gradient favors some compact arrangements over overbuilt relatives, not aromaticity or halogen content alone. Matched seed 0/1/2 final Top-1 values are Child 0.3940393921126993, 0.41429901422917714, 0.4514335070299504 versus Parent 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596, 0.438972502037081. Seed 0 is a tiny decrease, about 0.000012, not an exact tie; seed 1 decreases and seed 2 increases. The Parent leaders included cumulated/imino N-chloro chemistry, an N-fluorinated fused ring with hydroxamate-like substitution and an indole vicinal diketone. The Child seed-0 conventional amide nearly matches its Parent endpoint while other seeds retain different liabilities. These exceptions prevent attributing the endpoint differences to a single chemical motif.

per_task.generated_character: All evaluated optimizer proposals contain aromatic and ring-closure text. Mean SMILES length is 121.2 and maximum length 244, markedly reflecting large linked structures rather than absence of ring chemistry. Seed 0 evaluation 261 has 115 heavy-atom tokens: repeated fused nitrogen-dione units joined through aza-aromatic, alkene/imine and ester-bearing regions, with multiple halogenated side chains. Its accepted insert-atom lineage lengthens an already huge parent from evaluation 259; later evaluation 292 expands to 120 tokens and ties its score. Seed 2 evaluation 283 has 104 tokens, with an extended polyaryl/azaaryl network, aryl ethers and fused lactone-like carbonyl rings; it came from accepted crossover parents. By contrast, seed 1 evaluation 243 has 31 tokens: linked aza-aromatic rings, a thioamide, aryl bromine/chlorine and a carbon-chlorinated allylic ether. Its same-score relative at evaluation 251 instead contains O-Cl. The compact thioamide and the giant repeated-ring families are chemically different solutions, all actually evaluated and the first leaders admitted to survival.
liabilities: Repeated 104- to 120-token aromatic/heterocyclic graphs have substantial size, connectivity and synthetic-complexity liabilities; scores cannot be interpreted as medicinal plausibility.

O-Cl in a tied compact relative and activated halogenated ether/ester environments warrant local scrutiny. Ordinary carbon-bound aryl halogens and the carbon-chlorinated ether leader must remain distinct from direct O-Cl chemistry.
missing_features: The output lacks consistent access to compact feasible alternatives that retain useful linked heteroaromatic/carbonyl relationships without repeating many large regions; seed 1 shows that such scale is not unavoidable.
No evidence demonstrates synthetic tractability for the giant linked leaders or clean bond-environment substitutes for every favorable halogenated relative.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originated in n-c55c3d520a2c and was carried by the same-code n-62daf219c70a Parent. In the new n-7922cfd1903a panel, high-scoring accepted and retained structures include N-F, N-Cl, N-Br, O-Cl and unusual doubly carbon-unsaturated sulfur environments. Conventional secondary amide and carbon-bound-halogen leaders also occur; one compact O-Cl-free structure ties an O-Cl relative, and another fluorinated leader has only carbon-bound fluorine. These current Search-Seed observations at 300 evaluations per task establish conditional local liabilities, not a universal need to remove halogens or heteroatoms.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments while adapting favorable aromatic, amine and carbonyl frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide bond-environment-aware alternatives that preserve useful relationships learned from real local feedback, including ordinary carbon-bound halogens and available nitrogen centres. Evaluate plausible substitutions through the same authorized feedback, without assuming a blanket filter improves scores. The chemistry association neither identifies a responsible learner constituent nor transfers an earlier component finding to the joint tree selector.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The Parent inherited a geometry gap from n-c55c3d520a2c. Current accepted leaders again include very short carbon or oxygen bridges, crowded nitrogen/carbonyl ring systems and small unsaturated rings; low-scoring later relatives include cyclic cumulation and ring reorganizations. A compact conventional indole amide also remains favorable, and the Parent has a high-scoring unusual cyclic-cumulene exception. Thus strained-looking graphs are neither universally necessary nor uniformly penalized by the observed objectives.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generated ring graphs do not consistently establish credible bridge geometry, unsaturation or stereochemical identity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need size-, bridge- and bond-geometry awareness and feasible alternative connectivities that retain learned functional context. Preserve access to ordinary fused and saturated rings. Structural feasibility needs its own check; neither SMILES validity nor a high score establishes it, and these observations do not prove a score gain from any particular restriction.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This representation gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and its same-code Parent. Every current task again has stereocentre and formal-charge text incidence 0.0 across its 870 evaluated optimizer proposals, although saturated fluorinated centres, bridged centres and recognizable protonatable amines occur. The current score records do not compare stereoisomers or establish protonation or tautomer populations.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output leaves potentially stereogenic centres unspecified and does not establish the chemical microstates represented by neutral text.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or resolve stereochemical identity where chemically meaningful, treating achiral and configurationally unstable cases appropriately. Assess protonation and tautomer identity separately from charge-marker absence; do not infer that neutral strings lack basic nitrogen. This is an identity/coverage limitation with no measured score penalty or isolated model attribution.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The original n-c55c3d520a2c gap, reproduced in n-62daf219c70a, included both fragmentation and overgrowth. The current panel changes its emphasis: two endpoint leaders contain 104 and 115 heavy-atom tokens, and a 120-token relative exactly ties the latter, while a 31-token leader in the same objective is also favorable. Elsewhere 48-, 51-, 59- and 64-token linked structures score poorly compared with compact leaders. Rings and aromatic text are almost universal in this panel, so the older tiny-fragment observation must not be generalized into a current absence of aromatic context.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably control excessive elaboration while retaining the functional context of useful compact molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use real feedback to preserve useful multi-region context while offering simplifications and nonduplicative replacements. The missing capability is consistent context-sensitive control, not the ability to make either small molecules or large rings. Do not infer a universal size cutoff, score advantage for compactness, or causal responsibility of bootstrap trees from these whole-node observations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The coverage gap originated in n-c55c3d520a2c and was repeated in the same-code Parent. Current leaders within a seed often vary side-chain length, halogen identity, one ring atom or bridge connectivity; several distinct structures tie raw endpoints. Across seeds there are nevertheless compact amides, linked thioamides, very large polyaryl systems, cyclic amines and nitrogen-carbonyl frameworks, so global structural collapse is unsupported. The accepted provenance shows real exposure and survival for the quoted leaders, not a catalogue of all unselected pool chemistry or independent efficacies.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently supply chemically independent, plausible alternatives within each leading family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Develop feasible scaffold replacements that retain task-local favorable chemical relationships, then assess their real accepted outcomes. Distinct SMILES, finite folded-count identities, equal predictions or shared tree leaves are not measures of chemically independent coverage. Unscored mean or alternative-tree choices cannot supply a counterfactual chemistry benefit; keep the original source and these applicability conditions with this gap.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

original_finding.headline: Generation-order allocation loses 0.124388 in mean endpoint score despite retaining full pool and model effort.
original_finding.insights:
This closes a different question from the earlier count, residual and correlation controls: allocating evaluations using the complete predictive selector matters even when generation effort is held at the inherited full-pool boundary. The earlier selector addition also enlarged the pool and lacked a complete matched Parent panel, so it could not establish this conditional contrast. Local parent beats increased from 629 to 653, yet incumbent improvements fell from 258 to 163; adaptive local success is not a substitute for endpoint quality. The present loss does not apportion value among posterior means, counts, residual amplitude or correlation, and separate sibling losses cannot be added.

A plausible place to investigate the loss is how evaluation choices preserve useful chemical relationships across adaptive histories. The molecular report finds that generation-order output still reaches useful nitrile and aryl-amine alternatives, including both improved endpoints, while other streams move into densely connected heteroatom frameworks and miss strong Parent families. Reactive bonds, questionable ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry persist. This concerns the evaluated distribution; it does not show that better alternatives were absent from the complete pools or identify a chemical mediator. Passive alternatives have no counterfactual scores.

Removing predictive influence is also different from removing computational cost: all surplus generation and model computations remain, and numerical failures would still use the inherited routes. No reduced-pool, compute-saving or optimizer-deletion conclusion follows. Actual recovery branches remain unexercised despite passing deterministic synthetic checks.

The passive original sampler selected a different set in all 435 batches, and its sampled values strictly preferred another candidate on 4,317 of 4,350 generation-order masks. Thus the removal changed real evaluation choices under strong exposure. original_finding.headline: Learned episode heads diversify real choices and molecular distances, but lower the aggregate score
original_finding.insights: Scarce feedback was sufficient to produce distinct learned head policies that changed real multistep search. The receipts rule out unused network copies, numerical value offsets alone, mask regeneration and broken feedback handling as explanations for this run. The exploration effect also appeared in average fingerprint distances, yet the large docking-score loss outweighed gains on three tasks. Greater policy and state diversity therefore did not deliver a higher aggregate score in this test. The molecular assessment still finds concentrated high-scoring families, reactive heteroatom motifs and demanding short bridges. The docking decline accompanies a different nitrogen, bridge and sulfur arrangement, which is an observed association rather than an identified causal structural defect. Broader fingerprint movement has not yet established broader coverage of useful, practical scaffold families. Further evidence is needed to separate the contributions of independent initialization, masked learning and persistent head identity, and to estimate score reliability across seeds. These results come from one paired screening seed; they do not establish a general score penalty or calibrated uncertainty.
original_finding.results: The heads learned from different persistent transition subsets and kept their assigned identities through all 250 molecular editing episodes. Of 1070 exploitation decisions after learning, 710 strictly preferred an edit outside head zero’s maximizing choices; every episode offered multiple exploitation decisions under its persistent head. Mean molecular fingerprint distance from episode starts rose from 0.443448 to 0.489426, and distance between contemporaneous lane states rose from 0.681615 to 0.733227. Later episode-best gains following losses increased from 123 to 145 events, although their mean positive increment fell from 0.015693 to 0.010788. The single-seed evaluator macro Top-1 score fell from 0.406693 to 0.350704, a change of -0.055989. Task Top-1 scores changed as follows: zaleplon_mpo 0.332184 to 0.438122 (+0.105938); deco_hop 0.614535 to 0.621204 (+0.006669); drd2_docking 0.753647 to 0.301684 (-0.451962); median_2 0.195125 to 0.184354 (-0.010772); sitagliptin_mpo 0.137973 to 0.208154 (+0.070181). All five tasks completed their 300-evaluation budgets with no invalid or duplicate proposals.

original_finding.headline: Accepted-error scaling changes choices and intervals but lowers the matched endpoint mean by 0.038141
original_finding.insights: This feedback-amplitude variant is an executed but unsuccessful endpoint intervention; it does not overturn the separate evidence for retaining nonzero correlated residuals. Changing interval coverage and many selected identities is insufficient to establish useful search or calibration away from the acquired stream. Shrinkage and capped contributions preserve bounded adaptation, but 382 large errors remain in the Child diagnostics, and a common multiplier cannot anticipate a first unseen surprise. One shared first-batch miss is 253 raw allocation SDs from its prediction while the multiplier is still one. Which changed choices produce the losses remains unresolved. Molecular evidence preserves conventional alternatives and some larger improving ring families alongside reactive bond environments, crowded geometry, excessive elaboration and fragments. Those mixed examples rule out a universal size, ring or heteroatom rule as the explanation for the score loss. The next scientific question is which conditions make amplitude changes useful; these results do not justify re-tuning the preregistered constants after seeing the panel or combining sibling effects.

original_finding.headline: Incumbent targeting raises sampled batch utility, but smaller real gains lower all three seed means
original_finding.insights:
The experiment exposes a failure of the complete incumbent-referenced allocation rule under this Parent: correct positive-improvement targeting and higher sampled utility did not deliver larger real advances. More update events again accompanied smaller increments. The mean realized batch-improvement contrast telescopes to the final-score contrast on these equal-length streams, so those two failures should not be counted as independent endpoint evidence. The result supports a negative contribution from this whole rule under the tested composition. A threshold-only endpoint effect remains unresolved because the current unthresholded comparison has no separately evaluated future trajectory.

Finite-panel zero gain also failed to identify unproductive molecules. Fourteen zero-gain choices beat their frozen real incumbent, eleven made sequential incumbent updates, 205 were later bred and 119 survived to the final populations. Two became session leaders. Every one of those fourteen real wins had no sampled scenario above the incumbent. The chemical report includes a ring-free urea/enamide/thiocarbonyl leader and a distinct aza-dicarbonyl leader in this group. These are concrete limits of the sampled improvement support; they do not establish whether model error, finite tail sampling, myopic selection or later breeding caused the overall loss.

Selected-stream MSE and interval coverage improved while within-batch ordering weakened, but the selected molecules and histories changed. Those diagnostics do not establish repaired uncertainty or improved chemistry. Familiar amines and lactams still coexist with reactive bonds, difficult rings, large assemblies and unspecified stereochemistry. The older unthresholded and antithetic failures retain their exchange-containing Parent conditions, and shared-Parent siblings supply no isolated threshold, additive or joint-component effect. The complete exposed endpoint failure supplies the registered approach-review evidence without authorizing acquisition tuning.
original_finding.results:
The allocation mechanism executed and changed real decisions. All 435 frozen incumbents, 128-row posterior panels and 4,350 exact greedy choices passed independent reconstruction. There were 3,681 positive-gain choices and 669 exact-zero choices; 23 complete batches had zero sampled improvement from their first position. Every zero choice followed the registered smallest-index tie rule without a fallback. All 435 selected sets differed from the Parent rule on the same panels. Mean sampled batch-improvement utility rose by 0.005726: 371 batches improved, 64 tied and none declined. Against the unthresholded shared-panel rule, 343 sets changed and mean utility rose by 0.000256, with fifteen contrary losses.

Real progress moved the other way. Average realized batch improvement fell from 0.013351 to 0.011410. Advancing batches rose from 202 to 204 and sequential incumbent updates from 258 to 270, but mean positive batch gain fell from 0.028751 to 0.024331. Mean accepted offspring score also fell, from 0.385256 to 0.351177. All evaluations completed, yet final mean score fell from 0.595670 to 0.539394, a paired change of -0.056276 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were -0.092867, -0.016706 and -0.059254. Nine task-seed endpoints declined and six improved, including all three median-similarity endpoints.

original_finding.headline: Rank targets change every selected batch but reduce ordering correlation and mean endpoint score
original_finding.insights: The missing benefit is not explained by an unexposed transformation or unchanged choices: ordinal targets alter the entire panel, but their registered ordering advantage fails. Preserving observed label order is insufficient to preserve useful cardinal spacing or improve prediction on newly selected molecules. Even so, all three median_2 endpoints improve while their ordering correlations worsen, and raw parent beats and incumbent gains rise from 629/258 to 655/272 despite the lower overall endpoint mean. Those counterexamples prevent treating ordering correlation or local gains as complete explanations of search utility. Six distinct-molecule pool pairs still share both folded and native count vectors. Conventional aryl amines and carbonyl families remain useful alongside reactive bonds, complex rings and unspecified stereochemistry; target remapping does not repair those chemistry or identity limits. Latent uncertainty has no established raw-score calibration, and no raw-unit error or coverage proxy is substituted. This is a negative result for the rank-target increment on this composition, while the earlier positive evidence for the composite selector remains intact; the role of lost cardinal gaps and later adaptive paths is unresolved.

original_finding.headline: Unfolding changes covariance and selection but lowers every seed’s macro score
original_finding.insights: The experiment rules out insufficient representation or allocation exposure as an explanation for the missing gain. Removing folding changes ordinary similarity relationships and adaptive choices, but it does not reliably help the retained optimizer. On the same Child selected molecules, prediction MSE improves only slightly, from 0.007847 to 0.007808, and interval coverage rises from 75.36% to 75.82%; those diagnostics do not rescue the endpoint result. All three median_2 streams worsen in prediction MSE while improving at the endpoint, further limiting a simple prediction-to-search explanation. Exact native-count ties remain, as do finite-hash and local-environment limits. The molecular output retains useful aromatic, amine, urea and carbonyl organization alongside reactive bonds, crowded rings and unspecified stereochemistry; neither the losses nor the median_2 gains establish a universal size or chemical-feasibility rule. This is a negative result for the incremental unfolding variant on this composition, not a reversal of the earlier evidence for retaining occurrence counts. Changed means and covariance, adaptive graph paths and possible lost accidental regularization remain unresolved mediators.
original_finding.results: Native counts preserve multiplicity and remove modulo-bin mixing on 41,278 of 69,600 pool occurrences. All 435 pool kernels change against their folded controls, changing 392 selected sets while 43 sets remain identical. Nine distinct-molecule pairs still share native count vectors. Every active fit and choice reconstructs, and every evaluation completes. Mean endpoint score falls from 0.595670 to 0.547507, a decrease of 0.048163 rather than the required 0.002 increase. Seed macro changes are -0.077453, -0.013541 and -0.053495. Six task-seed endpoints improve and nine decline; all three median_2 endpoints improve. Macro dispersion drops from 0.026593 to 0.000322 around the lower mean.

original_finding.headline: Atom-pair information changed search and split six local aliases, but the mean endpoint fell by 0.033408
original_finding.insights: More descriptor distinctions and better predictions on selected molecules did not yield better endpoint search in this fixed mixture. On the actual accepted stream, raw MSE improved from 0.009475 for the passive local model to 0.009335, and mean batch ordering correlation rose from 0.545819 to 0.571243, despite the endpoint loss. These improvements were uneven: MSE worsened in seven task/seed cells, including all median_2 cells. Ordinary similarity and regularization changes were broadly exposed, whereas alias-mediated benefit was not: ten members of five split pool pairs remained unscored, and only one member of the cross pair was evaluated. Thirteen other pairs shared atom-pair counts but remained distinguishable through local counts; the channels still do not establish complete molecular identity. The negative result belongs to this one equal-weight composition and does not undo the earlier evidence for retaining local occurrence counts or isolate atom-pair information from mixture weighting. Molecular evidence still shows reactive heteroatom-halogen and sulfur motifs, large linked assemblies and destructive fragments alongside conventional high-scoring chemistry. Added topological information does not enforce chemical feasibility, and neither a universal size explanation nor an alias-resolution explanation is established.
original_finding.results: All 435 batches changed their raw posterior means, uncertainties and conditional covariance. Against the same-input local-only reference, 432 selected sets and 433 orders changed; three sets and two orders remained unchanged. All six distinct local-count alias pairs split, but none had both members scored. All three matched replicas completed. Mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.562261, a loss of 0.033408 against the required gain of 0.002. Seed deltas were −0.072325, +0.009185 and −0.037084. Six of fifteen task/seed endpoints improved: all three zaleplon results and the seed-1 deco_hop, drd2 and sitagliptin results. Every median_2 result declined. Seed dispersion decreased from 0.026593 to 0.006995 around the lower mean. The mechanism ran correctly; its registered endpoint-benefit prediction was falsified.

original_finding.headline: Generation-order allocation loses 0.124388 in mean endpoint score despite retaining full pool and model effort.
original_finding.insights:
This closes a different question from the earlier count, residual and correlation controls: allocating evaluations using the complete predictive selector matters even when generation effort is held at the inherited full-pool boundary. The earlier selector addition also enlarged the pool and lacked a complete matched Parent panel, so it could not establish this conditional contrast. Local parent beats increased from 629 to 653, yet incumbent improvements fell from 258 to 163; adaptive local success is not a substitute for endpoint quality. The present loss does not apportion value among posterior means, counts, residual amplitude or correlation, and separate sibling losses cannot be added.

A plausible place to investigate the loss is how evaluation choices preserve useful chemical relationships across adaptive histories. The molecular report finds that generation-order output still reaches useful nitrile and aryl-amine alternatives, including both improved endpoints, while other streams move into densely connected heteroatom frameworks and miss strong Parent families. Reactive bonds, questionable ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry persist. This concerns the evaluated distribution; it does not show that better alternatives were absent from the complete pools or identify a chemical mediator. Passive alternatives have no counterfactual scores.

Removing predictive influence is also different from removing computational cost: all surplus generation and model computations remain, and numerical failures would still use the inherited routes. No reduced-pool, compute-saving or optimizer-deletion conclusion follows. Actual recovery branches remain unexercised despite passing deterministic synthetic checks.

Thus the removal changed real evaluation choices under strong exposure. All 435 fits, full covariance factorizations and original normal arrays remained computed; the accepted-only feedback and identity-bound prediction joins passed. original_finding.headline: Learned episode heads diversify real choices and molecular distances, but lower the aggregate score
original_finding.insights: Scarce feedback was sufficient to produce distinct learned head policies that changed real multistep search. The receipts rule out unused network copies, numerical value offsets alone, mask regeneration and broken feedback handling as explanations for this run. The exploration effect also appeared in average fingerprint distances, yet the large docking-score loss outweighed gains on three tasks. Greater policy and state diversity therefore did not deliver a higher aggregate score in this test. The molecular assessment still finds concentrated high-scoring families, reactive heteroatom motifs and demanding short bridges. The docking decline accompanies a different nitrogen, bridge and sulfur arrangement, which is an observed association rather than an identified causal structural defect. Broader fingerprint movement has not yet established broader coverage of useful, practical scaffold families. Further evidence is needed to separate the contributions of independent initialization, masked learning and persistent head identity, and to estimate score reliability across seeds. These results come from one paired screening seed; they do not establish a general score penalty or calibrated uncertainty.

original_finding.insights: This feedback-amplitude variant is an executed but unsuccessful endpoint intervention; it does not overturn the separate evidence for retaining nonzero correlated residuals. Changing interval coverage and many selected identities is insufficient to establish useful search or calibration away from the acquired stream. Shrinkage and capped contributions preserve bounded adaptation, but 382 large errors remain in the Child diagnostics, and a common multiplier cannot anticipate a first unseen surprise. One shared first-batch miss is 253 raw allocation SDs from its prediction while the multiplier is still one. Which changed choices produce the losses remains unresolved. Those mixed examples rule out a universal size, ring or heteroatom rule as the explanation for the score loss. The next scientific question is which conditions make amplitude changes useful; these results do not justify re-tuning the preregistered constants after seeing the panel or combining sibling effects.

original_finding.headline: Incumbent targeting raises sampled batch utility, but smaller real gains lower all three seed means
original_finding.insights:
The experiment exposes a failure of the complete incumbent-referenced allocation rule under this Parent: correct positive-improvement targeting and higher sampled utility did not deliver larger real advances. More update events again accompanied smaller increments. The mean realized batch-improvement contrast telescopes to the final-score contrast on these equal-length streams, so those two failures should not be counted as independent endpoint evidence. The result supports a negative contribution from this whole rule under the tested composition. A threshold-only endpoint effect remains unresolved because the current unthresholded comparison has no separately evaluated future trajectory.

Finite-panel zero gain also failed to identify unproductive molecules. Fourteen zero-gain choices beat their frozen real incumbent, eleven made sequential incumbent updates, 205 were later bred and 119 survived to the final populations. Two became session leaders. Every one of those fourteen real wins had no sampled scenario above the incumbent. The chemical report includes a ring-free urea/enamide/thiocarbonyl leader and a distinct aza-dicarbonyl leader in this group. These are concrete limits of the sampled improvement support; they do not establish whether model error, finite tail sampling, myopic selection or later breeding caused the overall loss.

Selected-stream MSE and interval coverage improved while within-batch ordering weakened, but the selected molecules and histories changed. Those diagnostics do not establish repaired uncertainty or improved chemistry. Familiar amines and lactams still coexist with reactive bonds, difficult rings, large assemblies and unspecified stereochemistry. The older unthresholded and antithetic failures retain their exchange-containing Parent conditions, and shared-Parent siblings supply no isolated threshold, additive or joint-component effect. The complete exposed endpoint failure supplies the registered approach-review evidence without authorizing acquisition tuning.
original_finding.results:
The allocation mechanism executed and changed real decisions. All 435 frozen incumbents, 128-row posterior panels and 4,350 exact greedy choices passed independent reconstruction. There were 3,681 positive-gain choices and 669 exact-zero choices; 23 complete batches had zero sampled improvement from their first position. Every zero choice followed the registered smallest-index tie rule without a fallback. All 435 selected sets differed from the Parent rule on the same panels. Against the unthresholded shared-panel rule, 343 sets changed and mean utility rose by 0.000256, with fifteen contrary losses.

Real progress moved the other way. Average realized batch improvement fell from 0.013351 to 0.011410. Advancing batches rose from 202 to 204 and sequential incumbent updates from 258 to 270, but mean positive batch gain fell from 0.028751 to 0.024331. Mean accepted offspring score also fell, from 0.385256 to 0.351177. All evaluations completed, yet final mean score fell from 0.595670 to 0.539394, a paired change of -0.056276 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were -0.092867, -0.016706 and -0.059254. Nine task-seed endpoints declined and six improved, including all three median-similarity endpoints.

original_finding.headline: Rank targets change every selected batch but reduce ordering correlation and mean endpoint score
original_finding.insights: The missing benefit is not explained by an unexposed transformation or unchanged choices: ordinal targets alter the entire panel, but their registered ordering advantage fails. Preserving observed label order is insufficient to preserve useful cardinal spacing or improve prediction on newly selected molecules. Even so, all three median_2 endpoints improve while their ordering correlations worsen, and raw parent beats and incumbent gains rise from 629/258 to 655/272 despite the lower overall endpoint mean. Those counterexamples prevent treating ordering correlation or local gains as complete explanations of search utility. Six distinct-molecule pool pairs still share both folded and native count vectors. Conventional aryl amines and carbonyl families remain useful alongside reactive bonds, complex rings and unspecified stereochemistry; target remapping does not repair those chemistry or identity limits. Latent uncertainty has no established raw-score calibration, and no raw-unit error or coverage proxy is substituted. This is a negative result for the rank-target increment on this composition, while the earlier positive evidence for the composite selector remains intact; the role of lost cardinal gaps and later adaptive paths is unresolved.

original_finding.headline: Unfolding changes covariance and selection but lowers every seed’s macro score
original_finding.insights: The experiment rules out insufficient representation or allocation exposure as an explanation for the missing gain. Removing folding changes ordinary similarity relationships and adaptive choices, but it does not reliably help the retained optimizer. On the same Child selected molecules, prediction MSE improves only slightly, from 0.007847 to 0.007808, and interval coverage rises from 75.36% to 75.82%; those diagnostics do not rescue the endpoint result. All three median_2 streams worsen in prediction MSE while improving at the endpoint, further limiting a simple prediction-to-search explanation. Exact native-count ties remain, as do finite-hash and local-environment limits. The molecular output retains useful aromatic, amine, urea and carbonyl organization alongside reactive bonds, crowded rings and unspecified stereochemistry; neither the losses nor the median_2 gains establish a universal size or chemical-feasibility rule. This is a negative result for the incremental unfolding variant on this composition, not a reversal of the earlier evidence for retaining occurrence counts. Changed means and covariance, adaptive graph paths and possible lost accidental regularization remain unresolved mediators.
original_finding.results: Native counts preserve multiplicity and remove modulo-bin mixing on 41,278 of 69,600 pool occurrences. All 435 pool kernels change against their folded controls, changing 392 selected sets while 43 sets remain identical. Nine distinct-molecule pairs still share native count vectors. Every active fit and choice reconstructs, and every evaluation completes. Mean endpoint score falls from 0.595670 to 0.547507, a decrease of 0.048163 rather than the required 0.002 increase. Seed macro changes are -0.077453, -0.013541 and -0.053495. Six task-seed endpoints improve and nine decline; all three median_2 endpoints improve. Macro dispersion drops from 0.026593 to 0.000322 around the lower mean.

original_finding.headline: Atom-pair information changed search and split six local aliases, but the mean endpoint fell by 0.033408
original_finding.insights: More descriptor distinctions and better predictions on selected molecules did not yield better endpoint search in this fixed mixture. On the actual accepted stream, raw MSE improved from 0.009475 for the passive local model to 0.009335, and mean batch ordering correlation rose from 0.545819 to 0.571243, despite the endpoint loss. These improvements were uneven: MSE worsened in seven task/seed cells, including all median_2 cells. Ordinary similarity and regularization changes were broadly exposed, whereas alias-mediated benefit was not: ten members of five split pool pairs remained unscored, and only one member of the cross pair was evaluated. Thirteen other pairs shared atom-pair counts but remained distinguishable through local counts; the channels still do not establish complete molecular identity. The negative result belongs to this one equal-weight composition and does not undo the earlier evidence for retaining local occurrence counts or isolate atom-pair information from mixture weighting. Molecular evidence still shows reactive heteroatom-halogen and sulfur motifs, large linked assemblies and destructive fragments alongside conventional high-scoring chemistry. Added topological information does not enforce chemical feasibility, and neither a universal size explanation nor an alias-resolution explanation is established.

finding_summary.headline: Tree functions changed every selected batch, but the paired endpoint mean fell by 0.060977
finding_summary.insights:
Distinct fitted functions and changed evaluation choices were not sufficient for endpoint benefit. Selected-stream mean squared error improved from 0.012718 to 0.010939, while ordering correlation fell from 0.5322 to 0.4474. Every median_2 error improved even though all its endpoints declined. These are different adaptive evaluation streams, so neither the lower error nor the empirical tree spread establishes calibration or explains the total loss. Exact ties, leaf-average support and later search history remain possible contributors whose individual effects were not isolated.

The inherited inputs still merge some distinct molecules: nineteen current alias pairs were observed, but only one pair had both members scored, at an equal value. Trees additionally give equal predictions to many unequal count vectors. Neither representation aliases nor shared leaves prove chemical identity or independent scaffold coverage. Conventional compact indole amides, carbon-bound halogens and available amines coexist with giant linked-ring structures, reactive bonds and difficult bridges. Useful conventional counterexamples rule out a universal need for those liabilities; they do not establish a chemical cause of the score loss.

This result concerns the joint fixed learner and sampled-function law. It does not reverse the useful GP boundary or its conditional component findings, and it does not identify separate effects of trees, bootstrapping, ties or uncertainty. The large runtime spread is preserved: all replicas completed under identical resources, with much of the observed elapsed variation in deco_hop oracle time. Changed molecules and nested instrumentation prevent an isolated learner-speed or chemistry attribution.

The inherited inputs still merge some distinct molecules: nineteen current alias pairs were observed, but only one pair had both members scored, at an equal value. Trees additionally give equal predictions to many unequal count vectors. Neither representation aliases nor shared leaves prove chemical identity or independent scaffold coverage. Conventional compact indole amides, carbon-bound halogens and available amines coexist with giant linked-ring structures, reactive bonds and difficult bridges. Useful conventional counterexamples rule out a universal need for those liabilities; they do not establish a chemical cause of the score loss.

This result concerns the joint fixed learner and sampled-function law.
